sentences.zh: 何文輝

translations.literal: He Wenhui
translations.idiomatic: He Wenhui

sentences.zh: 何文輝，字德明，滁人。

translations.literal: He Wenhui, styled Deming, was a man of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Wenhui, whose courtesy name was Deming, came from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖下滁州，得文輝，年十四，撫為己子，賜姓硃氏。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor took Chuzhou, he obtained Wenhui, who was fourteen years old, raised him as his own son, and granted him the surname Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor captured Chuzhou, he took in Wenhui at the age of fourteen, treated him as his own son, and gave him the Zhu surname.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，多蓄義子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the founding emperor's rise, he kept many adopted sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days of his rise, the founding emperor adopted many sons.

sentences.zh: 及長，命偕諸將分守諸路。

translations.literal: When they grew up, he ordered them together with the generals to guard the various routes separately.
translations.idiomatic: Once they came of age, he sent them out with his generals to hold the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 周舍守鎮江，道舍守寧國，馬兒守婺州，柴舍、真童守處州，金剛奴守衢州，皆義子也。

translations.literal: Zhou She guarded Zhenjiang, Dao She guarded Ningguo, Ma Er guarded Wuzhou, Chai She and Zhen Tong guarded Chuzhou, and Jingang Nu guarded Quzhou—all were adopted sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She held Zhenjiang, Dao She held Ningguo, Ma Er held Wuzhou, Chai She and Zhen Tong held Chuzhou, and Jingang Nu held Quzhou; all were his adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 金剛奴後無考。

translations.literal: Nothing further is recorded of Jingang Nu.
translations.idiomatic: No further account survives for Jingang Nu.

sentences.zh: 周舍即沐英，軍中又呼沐舍。

translations.literal: Zhou She was Mu Ying; in the army he was also called Mu She.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She was Mu Ying, whom the troops also called Mu She.

sentences.zh: 柴舍者，硃文剛，與耿再成死處州難。

translations.literal: Chai She was Zhu Wengang, who died with Geng Zaicheng in the disaster at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chai She was Zhu Wengang, who perished with Geng Zaicheng in the calamity at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又有硃文遜，史不傳其小字，亦以義子死太平。

translations.literal: There was also Zhu Wensun, whose childhood name the histories do not record; he too died at Taiping as an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhu Wensun, whose childhood name is not recorded in the histories; he likewise died at Taiping in service as an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 自沐英外，最著者唯道舍、馬兒，馬兒即徐司馬，而道舍即文輝也。

translations.literal: Apart from Mu Ying, the most renowned were only Dao She and Ma Er; Ma Er was Xu Sima, and Dao She was Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Mu Ying, the most prominent were Dao She and Ma Er—Ma Er being Xu Sima, and Dao She being Wenhui himself.

sentences.zh: 文輝以天寧翼元帥守寧國，進江西行省參政。

translations.literal: Wenhui, as Tianning Vice Marshal, guarded Ningguo and was promoted to Jiangxi Branch Secretariat Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui served as Tianning Vice Marshal defending Ningguo, then rose to become Vice Administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 數攻江西，未下州縣。

translations.literal: He attacked Jiangxi repeatedly but did not reduce the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Jiangxi several times but could not bring its prefectures and counties to submission.

sentences.zh: 討新淦鄧仲廉，斬之。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Deng Zhonglian of Xingan and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Deng Zhonglian of Xingan and executed him.

sentences.zh: 援安福，走饒鼎臣，平山尖寨。

translations.literal: He relieved Anfu, drove off Rao Dingchen, and pacified the Shanjian stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Anfu, put Rao Dingchen to flight, and pacified the Shanjian stockade.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取淮東，復從下平江。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Huaidong, then followed again in reducing Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in the conquest of Huaidong and again in the reduction of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 賜文綺，進行省左丞，復其姓。

translations.literal: He was granted patterned silks, promoted to Branch Secretariat Left Vice Administrator, and restored to his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: He received gifts of patterned silk, was promoted to Left Vice Administrator of the branch secretariat, and had his original surname restored.

sentences.zh: 以征南副將軍與平章胡美由江西取福建，度杉關，入光澤，徇邵武、建陽，直趨建寧。

translations.literal: As Southern Campaign Deputy General, together with Pacification Commissioner Hu Mei he took Fujian from Jiangxi, crossed Shanguan Pass, entered Guangze, subdued Shaowu and Jianyang, and pressed straight on Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: As Deputy General of the Southern Campaign, he joined Pacification Commissioner Hu Mei in taking Fujian from Jiangxi, crossed Shanguan Pass, entered Guangze, subdued Shaowu and Jianyang, and marched directly on Jianning.

sentences.zh: 元同僉達里麻、參政陳子琦閉門拒守。

translations.literal: The Yuan Vice Commissioner Dalima and Administrator Chen Ziqi shut the gates and resisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Vice Commissioner Dalima and Administrator Chen Ziqi barred the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 文輝與美環攻之。

translations.literal: Wenhui and Mei besieged and attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui and Mei laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 逾十日，達里麻不能支，夜潛至文輝營，乞降。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Dalima could not hold out; at night he stole into Wenhui's camp and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days Dalima could no longer hold out; he slipped into Wenhui's camp by night and asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，總管翟也先不花亦以眾降於文輝。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, Commander-in-Chief Zhaye Xianbuhua also surrendered with his troops to Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the next morning, Commander-in-Chief Zhaye Xianbuhua also came over to Wenhui with his forces.

sentences.zh: 美怒兩人不詣己，欲屠其城。

translations.literal: Mei was angry that the two men had not come to him and wished to slaughter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was furious that neither man had come to him and wanted to massacre the city.

sentences.zh: 文輝馳告美曰：「與公同受命至此，為安百姓耳。

translations.literal: Wenhui hurried to tell Mei, saying: "You and I received orders together to come here in order to bring peace to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui rode at once to tell Mei, "We were both sent here on the same mission—to bring peace to the people.

sentences.zh: 今既降，奈何以私忿殺人。」

translations.literal: Now that they have surrendered, how can we kill people because of private anger?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have submitted, how can we slaughter them over a private grudge?"

sentences.zh: 美乃止。

translations.literal: Mei then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mei relented.

sentences.zh: 師入城，秋毫無所犯。

translations.literal: When the army entered the city, not even a hair's breadth was violated.
translations.idiomatic: When the army entered the city, not the slightest harm was done to the populace.

sentences.zh: 汀、泉諸州縣聞之，皆相次歸附。

translations.literal: When the prefectures and counties of Ting and Quan heard of this, they all submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the prefectures and counties of Ting and Quan submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 會車駕幸汴梁，召文輝扈從，因命為河南衛指揮使，定汝州余寇。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage visited Bianliang; Wenhui was summoned to attend in escort and was thereupon appointed Commander of the Henan Guard to settle the remaining bandits of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Bianliang, Wenhui was summoned to join the retinue and was appointed Commander of the Henan Guard to pacify the remaining rebels in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍取陝西，留守潼關。

translations.literal: He followed the Great General in taking Shaanxi and remained to guard Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Great General in the conquest of Shaanxi and was left to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，授大都督府都督僉事，予世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and granted a hereditary commandership.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he was made Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and granted a hereditary commandership.

sentences.zh: 復以參將從傅友德等平蜀，賜金幣，留守成都。

translations.literal: Again as deputy general he followed Fu Youde and others in pacifying Shu, was granted gold and coins, and remained to guard Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as deputy general under Fu Youde in the pacification of Shu, received gifts of gold and coin, and was left to garrison Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 文輝號令明肅，軍民皆德之。

translations.literal: Wenhui's orders were clear and strict; both army and people regarded him with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui's commands were clear and stern, and both soldiers and civilians held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗稱其謀略威望。

translations.literal: The emperor once praised his strategic ability and prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised his strategic talent and standing.

sentences.zh: 遷大都督府同知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Associate Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 五年命帥山東兵從李文忠出應昌。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to lead Shandong troops and follow Li Wenzhong out to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was ordered to lead Shandong troops and follow Li Wenzhong to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮北平。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to garrison Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to command at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 文忠北征，文輝督兵巡居庸關，以疾召還。

translations.literal: When Wenzhong campaigned north, Wenhui supervised troops patrolling Juyong Pass; he was recalled because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Wenzhong's northern campaign, Wenhui directed troops on patrol at Juyong Pass but was recalled when he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 九年六月卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of year 9, at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 遣官營葬滁州東沙河上，恤賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Officials were sent to arrange his burial on the eastern Sha River at Chuzhou, and condolence gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to bury him on the eastern Sha River at Chuzhou, and the condolence gifts were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 子環，成都護衛指揮使，征迤北陣歿。

translations.literal: His son Huan was Commander of the Chengdu Guard; he died in battle on a campaign to the far north.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan, Commander of the Chengdu Guard, fell in battle on a campaign to the far north.

sentences.zh: 附 徐司馬

translations.literal: Appended: Xu Sima
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Xu Sima

sentences.zh: 九年遷鎮河南。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to garrison Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was transferred to command Henan.

sentences.zh: 時新建北京於汴梁，號重地。

translations.literal: At that time the new Northern Capital had been established at Bianliang and was called a vital region.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new Northern Capital had been established at Bianliang and was regarded as a region of critical importance.

sentences.zh: 帝素賢司馬，特委任之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long regarded Sima as worthy and especially entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long held Sima in high regard and gave him special trust.

sentences.zh: 宋國公馮勝方練兵河南。

translations.literal: Duke of Song Feng Sheng was then drilling troops in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Song, Feng Sheng, was then training troops in Henan.

sentences.zh: 會有星變，占在大梁。

translations.literal: It happened that there was a change in the stars, and the omen pointed to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: A celestial anomaly appeared, and the omen was read as bearing on Daliang.

sentences.zh: 帝使使密敕勝，且曰：「並以此語馬兒知之。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy with a secret edict to Sheng, saying also: "Let Ma Er know this as well."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a secret edict to Sheng and added, "Let Ma Er know of this as well."

sentences.zh: 既復敕二人曰：「天象屢見，大梁軍民錯處，尤宜慎防。

translations.literal: He then again instructed the two men: "Heavenly signs have appeared repeatedly; in Daliang soldiers and civilians are intermingled, and you must be especially careful in your precautions.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent both men another instruction: "Heavenly signs have appeared again and again. In Daliang soldiers and civilians live side by side, and you must be especially vigilant.

sentences.zh: 今秦、晉二王還京，當嚴兵宿衛。

translations.literal: Now the Princes of Qin and Jin are returning to the capital; you should station troops in strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Qin and Jin are now returning to the capital. You must post troops in strict guard.

sentences.zh: 王抵汴時，若宋國公出迓，則都指揮居守；

translations.literal: When the princes reach Bian, if the Duke of Song goes out to welcome them, then the Regional Commander shall remain on guard;
translations.idiomatic: When the princes reach Bian, if the Duke of Song goes out to welcome them, the Regional Commander shall remain on guard;

sentences.zh: 都指揮出迓，則宋國公亦然。」

translations.literal: if the Regional Commander goes out to welcome them, then the Duke of Song shall do likewise."
translations.idiomatic: if the Regional Commander goes out to welcome them, the Duke of Song shall do the same."

sentences.zh: 敕書官而不名，倚重與宋公等。

translations.literal: The edicts named their offices but not their personal names, showing reliance equal to that on the Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The edicts referred to them by office rather than by name, placing the same trust in them as in the Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 十九年入覲，遂擢中軍都督府僉事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he came to court and was thereupon promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he presented himself at court and was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以左副總兵從藍玉征建昌，討越巂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief, he followed Lan Yu in campaigning against Jianchang and suppressing Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he served as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief under Lan Yu in the campaign against Jianchang and the suppression of Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 明年正月還至成都，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he returned to Chengdu and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Chengdu in the first month of the following year and died there.

sentences.zh: 追坐藍玉黨，二子皆獲罪。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was implicated as a member of Lan Yu's faction; both sons were punished.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was implicated in Lan Yu's faction; both his sons were punished.

sentences.zh: 司馬好文學，性謙厚，所至撫循士卒，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: Sima loved literature, was modest and generous by nature, and wherever he went comforted and guided the soldiers, winning the hearts of the troops greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Sima loved learning, was modest and generous by nature, and wherever he served won the troops' loyalty through his care for them.

sentences.zh: 在河南久，尤有惠政。

translations.literal: He was long in Henan and especially had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His long service in Henan was marked especially by benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 公暇退居，一室蕭然如寒素。

translations.literal: In his leisure after public duties he withdrew to his quarters; one room was austere as if he were a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In his off hours he retired to quarters as spare as those of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 雖戰功不及文輝，而雅量過之，並稱賢將雲。

translations.literal: Although his military achievements did not match Wenhui's, his magnanimity surpassed his, and both were called worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Though his battlefield record did not equal Wenhui's, his breadth of character surpassed his, and both were acclaimed as worthy generals.

sentences.zh: 葉旺

translations.literal: Ye Wang
translations.idiomatic: Ye Wang

translations.literal: Ma Yun]〉
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yun]〉

sentences.zh: 葉旺，六安人。

translations.literal: Ye Wang was a man of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Wang came from Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 與合肥人馬雲同隸長槍軍謝再興，為千戶。

translations.literal: Together with Ma Yun of Hefei he served under Xie Zaixing of the Long Spear Army as a chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ma Yun of Hefei both served under Xie Zaixing in the Long Spear Army as chiliarchs.

sentences.zh: 再興叛，二人自拔歸。

translations.literal: When Zaixing rebelled, the two men extricated themselves and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaixing rebelled, the two men broke away and rejoined the loyal forces.

sentences.zh: 數從征，積功並授指揮僉事。

translations.literal: They followed on several campaigns, accumulated merit, and were both appointed Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After several campaigns they had both earned merit and were appointed Vice Commanders.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，偕鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu they garrisoned Liaodong together.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 4 they were posted together to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 初，元主北走，其遼陽行省參政劉益屯蓋州，與平章高家奴相為聲援，保金、復等州。

translations.literal: At first, when the Yuan ruler fled north, his Liaoyang Branch Secretariat Administrator Liu Yi was stationed at Gaizhou, and together with Pacification Commissioner Gao Jianu they supported each other, holding Jin, Fu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Yuan ruler fled north, his Liaoyang Branch Secretariat Administrator Liu Yi held Gaizhou and, with Pacification Commissioner Gao Jianu as mutual support, kept Jin, Fu, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 帝遣斷事黃儔齎詔諭益。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the judicial commissioner Huang Chou bearing an edict to instruct Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Judicial Commissioner Huang Chou with an edict to summon Yi.

sentences.zh: 益籍所部兵馬、錢糧、輿地之數來歸。

translations.literal: Yi registered the numbers of his troops, horses, funds, grain, and territory under his command and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a register of his troops, horses, funds, grain, and territory and came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 乃立遼陽指揮使司，以益為指揮同知。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Liaoyang Command was established, with Yi as Associate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaoyang Command was then established, with Yi as Associate Commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元平章洪保保、馬彥翬合謀殺益。

translations.literal: Before long, the Yuan Pacification Commissioners Hong Baobao and Ma Yanhan conspired together to kill Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yuan Pacification Commissioners Hong Baobao and Ma Yanhan conspired to murder Yi.

sentences.zh: 右丞張良佐、左丞商暠擒彥翬殺之，保保挾儔走納哈出營。

translations.literal: Right Vice Administrator Zhang Liangzuo and Left Vice Administrator Shang Gao captured Yanhan and killed him; Baobao seized Chou and fled to Nahachu's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Administrator Zhang Liangzuo and Left Vice Administrator Shang Gao seized Yanhan and executed him; Baobao took Chou hostage and fled to Nahachu's camp.

sentences.zh: 良佐因權衛事，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Liangzuo thereupon assumed temporary authority over guard affairs and reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo assumed temporary command of guard affairs and reported the situation to the court.

sentences.zh: 且言：「遼東僻，處海隅，肘腋皆敵境。

translations.literal: He also said: "Liaodong is remote, situated on a corner of the sea; on every side at one's elbow and armpit are enemy territories.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote further: "Liaodong is remote, set on a coastal corner of the realm, with enemy territory on every side.

sentences.zh: 平章高家奴守遼陽山寨，知院哈剌章屯瀋陽古城，開元則右丞也先不花，金山則太尉納哈出。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Gao Jianu guards the Liaoyang mountain stockade; Court Commissioner Halazhang is stationed at the old city of Shenyang; at Kaiyuan is Right Vice Administrator Ye Xianbuhua; at Jinshan is Grand Marshal Nahachu.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Gao Jianu holds the Liaoyang mountain stockade; Court Commissioner Halazhang is posted at the old city of Shenyang; Kaiyuan is held by Right Vice Administrator Ye Xianbuhua; and Jinshan by Grand Marshal Nahachu.

sentences.zh: 彼此相依，時謀入犯。

translations.literal: They rely on one another and from time to time plot to invade.
translations.idiomatic: They support one another and from time to time plot incursions.

sentences.zh: 今保保逃往，釁必起。

translations.literal: Now that Baobao has fled there, trouble is certain to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Baobao has fled to them, hostilities are sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 乞留斷事吳立鎮撫軍民，而以所擒平章八丹、知院僧孺等械送京師。」

translations.literal: I beg to leave the judicial commissioner Wu Li to pacify the army and people, and to send the captured Pacification Commissioner Badan, Court Commissioner Sengru, and others in fetters to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Judicial Commissioner Wu Li be left to pacify the troops and people, and that the captured Pacification Commissioner Badan, Court Commissioner Sengru, and others be sent to the capital in bonds."

sentences.zh: 帝命立、良佐、暠俱為蓋州衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Li, Liangzuo, and Gao all as Vice Commanders of the Gaizhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Li, Liangzuo, and Gao all as Vice Commanders of the Gaizhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 既念遼陽重地，復設都指揮使司統轄諸衛，以旺及雲併為都指揮使往鎮之。

translations.literal: Considering further that Liaoyang was an important region, he re-established a Regional Military Commission to oversee the various guards and appointed Wang and Yun together as Regional Commanders to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Liaoyang was a region of critical importance, he re-established a Regional Military Commission to oversee the guards and sent Wang and Yun together as Regional Commanders to hold it.

sentences.zh: 已，知儔被殺，納哈出將內犯，敕旺等預為備。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was learned that Chou had been killed and that Nahachu was about to invade inland; Wang and the others were ordered to prepare defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Chou had been killed and that Nahachu was preparing an inland invasion; Wang and his colleagues were ordered to make ready in advance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，納哈出果以眾至，見備御嚴，不敢攻，越蓋至金州。

translations.literal: Before long Nahachu indeed came with a host; seeing the defenses strict, he did not dare attack but passed over Gaizhou and reached Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nahachu arrived with a large force; finding the defenses formidable, he did not attack but bypassed Gaizhou and marched on Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 金州城未完，指揮韋富、王勝等督士卒分守諸門。

translations.literal: The walls of Jinzhou were not yet complete; Commanders Wei Fu, Wang Sheng, and others directed the soldiers to guard the various gates separately.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou's walls were not yet finished; Commanders Wei Fu, Wang Sheng, and others directed the troops to hold the gates.

sentences.zh: 乃剌吾者，敵驍將也，率精騎數百挑戰城下，中伏弩僕，為我兵所獲。

translations.literal: Nailawu was a fierce enemy general; he led several hundred elite horsemen to challenge battle below the walls, was struck by ambush crossbows and fell, and was captured by our troops.
translations.idiomatic: Nailawu, a fierce enemy commander, led several hundred elite horsemen to challenge the city; he was struck down by ambush crossbows and captured by Ming troops.

sentences.zh: 敵大沮。

translations.literal: The enemy was greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 富等縱兵擊，敵引退，不敢由故道，從蓋城南十里沿柞河遁。

translations.literal: Fu and the others unleashed their troops in attack; the enemy withdrew, not daring to take the original route but fleeing along the Zha River ten li south of Gaizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his men sallied forth; the enemy retreated, afraid to take their original route, and fled along the Zha River ten li south of Gaizhou.

sentences.zh: 旺先以兵扼柞河。

translations.literal: Wang had beforehand stationed troops to block the Zha River.
translations.idiomatic: Wang had already posted troops to block the Zha River.

sentences.zh: 自連雲島至窟駝寨，十余里緣河壘冰為牆，沃以水，經宿凝沍如城。

translations.literal: From Lianyun Island to Kutuo Stockade, for more than ten li along the river they piled ice into a wall, poured water over it, and after one night it froze solid like a city wall.
translations.idiomatic: From Lianyun Island to Kutuo Stockade, for more than ten li along the river they built a wall of packed ice, poured water over it, and by the next morning it had frozen as hard as a city rampart.

sentences.zh: 布釘板沙中，旁設坑阱，伏兵以伺。

translations.literal: They laid nail boards in the sand and set pits and traps beside them, with ambush troops waiting.
translations.idiomatic: They set nail-studded boards in the sand, dug pits alongside, and posted ambush troops to wait.

sentences.zh: 雲及指揮周鶚、吳立等建大旗城中，嚴兵不動，寂若無人。

translations.literal: Yun and Commanders Zhou E, Wu Li, and others raised great banners in the city, kept the troops strict and unmoving, silent as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Commanders Zhou E and Wu Li raised great banners in the city and held their troops still, silent as if the city were empty.

sentences.zh: 已，寇至城南。

translations.literal: Presently the invaders reached the south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached the south of the city.

sentences.zh: 伏四起，兩山旌旗蔽空，矢石雨下。

translations.literal: Ambushes rose on four sides; on both mountains banners blotted out the sky, and arrows and stones rained down.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushes sprang up on every side; banners blotted out the sky on both hills, and arrows and stones rained down.

sentences.zh: 納哈出倉皇趨連雲島，遇冰城，旁走，悉陷於阱，遂大潰。

translations.literal: Nahachu in panic hurried toward Lianyun Island, met the ice wall, turned aside, and all fell into the traps; thereupon they collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Nahachu fled in panic toward Lianyun Island, struck the ice wall, turned aside, and his men fell wholesale into the traps; the army broke in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 雲自城中出，合兵追擊至將軍山、畢栗河，斬獲及凍死者無算，乘勝追至豬兒峪。

translations.literal: Yun came out from the city, joined forces in pursuit to General Mountain and the Bili River, and killed and captured and froze to death innumerable men; pressing the victory they pursued to Zhuer Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Yun sallied from the city and joined the pursuit to General Mountain and the Bili River; the slain, captured, and frozen to death were beyond count, and the victors pressed on to Zhuer Ravine.

sentences.zh: 納哈出僅以身免。

translations.literal: Nahachu alone escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: Nahachu alone escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 第功，進旺、雲俱都督僉事。

translations.literal: When merits were ranked, Wang and Yun were both promoted to Vice Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were assessed, Wang and Yun were both promoted to Vice Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時洪武八年也。

translations.literal: This was in the eighth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in Hongwu year 8.

sentences.zh: 十二年命雲征大寧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Yun was ordered to campaign against Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Yun was ordered to campaign against Daning.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，受賞，召還京。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, he received rewards and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he received rewards and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 旺留鎮如故。

translations.literal: Wang remained to garrison as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wang continued to hold his post as before.

sentences.zh: 會高麗遣使致書及禮物，而龍州鄭白等請內附。

translations.literal: It happened that Goryeo sent envoys with letters and gifts, while Zheng Bai of Longzhou and others requested to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys bearing letters and gifts, while Zheng Bai of Longzhou and others asked to submit to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 旺以聞。

translations.literal: Wang reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝謂：人臣無外交。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ministers must have no foreign dealings."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A subject must not conduct foreign relations on his own."

sentences.zh: 此間諜之漸，勿輕信。

translations.literal: This is the beginning of espionage; do not lightly trust it.
translations.idiomatic: This is how espionage begins—do not trust it lightly.

sentences.zh: 彼特示弱於我，以窺邊釁。

translations.literal: They are only showing weakness to us in order to spy out border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: They are only feigning weakness toward us to probe for a chance to strike the frontier.

sentences.zh: 還之，使無所藉口。

translations.literal: Send them back so they have no pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Send them back and give them no excuse for action.

sentences.zh: 明年，旺復送高麗使者周誼入京。

translations.literal: The next year Wang again sent the Goryeo envoy Zhou Yi to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang again escorted the Goryeo envoy Zhou Yi to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以其國中弒逆，又詭殺朝使，反覆不可信，切責旺等絕之，而留誼不遣。

translations.literal: The emperor, because their state had regicide and rebellion and had treacherously killed imperial envoys, was changeable and untrustworthy; he sharply rebuked Wang and the others to break relations and detained Yi without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, citing regicide and treachery in their kingdom and the murder of Ming envoys, declared them utterly untrustworthy; he sharply rebuked Wang and his colleagues for maintaining contact and detained Yi without returning him.

sentences.zh: 十九年召旺為後軍都督府僉事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Wang was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Wang was summoned to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 居三月，遼東有警，覆命還鎮。

translations.literal: After three months there was an alarm in Liaodong; he was again ordered to return and garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After three months an alarm arose in Liaodong, and he was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 二十一年三月卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of year 21.

sentences.zh: 旺與雲之鎮遼也，翦荊棘，立軍府，撫輯軍民，墾田萬余頃，遂為永利。

translations.literal: When Wang and Yun garrisoned Liaodong, they cut brambles, established military offices, comforted and gathered army and people, opened more than ten thousand qing of fields, and thereby made lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In garrisoning Liaodong, Wang and Yun cleared the wilderness, established military administration, pacified soldiers and civilians, and opened more than ten thousand qing of farmland, bringing lasting benefit to the region.

sentences.zh: 旺尤久，先後凡十七年。

translations.literal: Wang especially was there long, altogether seventeen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang served there the longest, seventeen years in all.

sentences.zh: 遼人德之。

translations.literal: The people of Liaodong regarded them with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liaodong held them in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，以二人有功於遼，命有司立祠，春秋祀之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, because the two men had merit in Liaodong, officials were ordered to erect a shrine and offer sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, because both men had rendered great service in Liaodong, the authorities were ordered to erect a shrine and offer sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 繆大亨

translations.literal: Miao Daheng
translations.idiomatic: Miao Daheng

sentences.zh: 繆大亨，定遠人。

translations.literal: Miao Daheng was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Daheng came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初糾義兵，為元攻濠，不克，元兵潰。

translations.literal: At first he gathered righteous troops and attacked Hao for the Yuan but did not take it; the Yuan army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He first raised a militia and attacked Hao on behalf of the Yuan but failed; the Yuan forces broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 大亨獨以眾二萬人與張知院屯橫澗山，固守月余。

translations.literal: Daheng alone with twenty thousand men and Court Commissioner Zhang encamped at Hengjian Mountain and held firm for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Daheng alone held Hengjian Mountain with twenty thousand men alongside Court Commissioner Zhang, defending stubbornly for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 太祖以計夜襲其營，破之，大亨與子走免。

translations.literal: The founding emperor by stratagem raided their camp at night, broke them, and Daheng escaped with his son.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor launched a night raid on their camp by stratagem, routed them, and Daheng escaped with his son.

sentences.zh: 比明，復收散卒，列陣以待。

translations.literal: By dawn he had again gathered scattered soldiers and arrayed ranks to await battle.
translations.idiomatic: By daybreak he had regathered his scattered troops and formed ranks to await the enemy.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣其叔貞諭降之，命將所部從征，數有功，擢元帥。

translations.literal: The founding emperor sent his uncle Zhen to instruct him to surrender, ordered him to lead his troops on campaign, and after several achievements promoted him to marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent his uncle Zhen to offer terms of surrender, then ordered him to lead his troops on campaign; after several victories he was promoted to marshal.

sentences.zh: 總兵取揚州，克之。

translations.literal: As commander-in-chief he took Yangzhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: As commander-in-chief he took and captured Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 降青軍元帥張明鑒。

translations.literal: He reduced the Green Army Marshal Zhang Mingjian.
translations.idiomatic: He induced the Green Army Marshal Zhang Mingjian to surrender.

sentences.zh: 初，明鑒聚眾淮西，以青布為號，稱「青軍」；

translations.literal: At first Mingjian gathered a host in Huaixi, used green cloth as his sign, and was called the "Green Army";
translations.idiomatic: Mingjian had first gathered followers in Huaixi, taking green cloth as his banner and calling his force the "Green Army";

sentences.zh: 又以善長槍，稱「長槍軍」。

translations.literal: because he was skilled with the long spear he was also called the "Long Spear Army."
translations.idiomatic: because they excelled with the long spear, they were also known as the "Long Spear Army."

sentences.zh: 由含山轉掠揚州，元鎮南王孛羅普化招降之，以為濠、泗義兵元帥。

translations.literal: From Hanshan they turned to plunder Yangzhou; the Yuan Prince of Zhennan Boluohuazhua recruited them to surrender and made them Righteous Troops Marshals of Hao and Si.
translations.idiomatic: They marched from Hanshan to plunder Yangzhou; the Yuan Prince of Zhennan Boluohuazhua induced them to submit and appointed them marshals of the righteous troops of Hao and Si.

sentences.zh: 逾年，食盡，謀擁王作亂。

translations.literal: After more than a year their food was exhausted and they plotted to seize the prince and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, with provisions exhausted, they plotted to seize the prince and rebel.

sentences.zh: 王走，死淮安。

translations.literal: The prince fled and died at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: The prince fled and died at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 明鑒遂據城，屠居民以食。

translations.literal: Mingjian thereupon seized the city and slaughtered the inhabitants for food.
translations.idiomatic: Mingjian then seized the city and slaughtered its inhabitants for food.

sentences.zh: 大亨言於太祖，賊飢困，若掠食四齣則難制矣，且驍鷙可用，無為他人得。

translations.literal: Daheng said to the founding emperor: "The bandits are hungry and trapped; if they go out to plunder food in all four directions they will be hard to control, and moreover they are fierce and can be used—do not let others get them."
translations.idiomatic: Daheng told the founding emperor, "The rebels are starving and cornered; if they scatter to plunder in all directions they will be hard to control. They are fierce fighters who can still be used—do not let another power take them."

sentences.zh: 太祖命大亨亟攻，明鑒降，得眾數萬、馬二千余匹。

translations.literal: The founding emperor ordered Daheng to attack urgently; Mingjian surrendered, and they obtained several tens of thousands of followers and more than two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor ordered Daheng to attack at once; Mingjian surrendered, yielding tens of thousands of followers and more than two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 悉送其將校妻子至應天。

translations.literal: All their officers' wives and children were sent to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: The wives and children of all their officers were sent to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 改淮海翼元帥府為江南分樞密院，以大亨為同僉樞密院事，總制揚州、鎮江。

translations.literal: The Huaihai Vice Marshal's headquarters was changed to the Jiangnan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs; Daheng was made Associate Commissioner and given overall control of Yangzhou and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaihai Vice Marshal's headquarters was converted to the Jiangnan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs; Daheng was appointed Associate Commissioner with overall authority over Yangzhou and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 大亨有治略，寬厚不擾，而治軍嚴肅，禁暴除殘，民甚悅之。

translations.literal: Daheng had governing ability, was generous and did not harass, yet governed the army with strict discipline, forbade violence and removed cruelty; the people were greatly pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Daheng had a gift for governance—lenient and unintrusive in civil affairs, yet strict in military discipline, suppressing violence and cruelty—and the people were deeply pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 太祖過鎮江，嘆曰：「繆將軍生平端直，未嘗有過，惜不見矣。」

translations.literal: When the founding emperor passed through Zhenjiang he sighed and said: "General Miao was upright all his life and never had a fault—it is a pity I shall not see him again."
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor passed through Zhenjiang, he sighed and said, "General Miao was upright all his life and never once erred—it is a pity I shall not see him again."

sentences.zh: 遣使祭其墓。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to sacrifice at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to offer sacrifices at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 附 武德

translations.literal: Appended: Wu De
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wu De

sentences.zh: 武德，安豐人。

translations.literal: Wu De was a man of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu De came from Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 元至正中為義兵千戶。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era of Yuan he was a righteous-troops chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan Zhizheng era he served as a chiliarch in the militia.

sentences.zh: 知元將亡，言於其帥張鑒曰：「吾輩才雄萬夫。

translations.literal: Knowing the Yuan was about to perish, he said to his commander Zhang Jian: "We are talents who dominate ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Yuan dynasty was doomed, he said to his commander Zhang Jian, "We are men whose talents match ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 今東衄西挫，事勢可知。

translations.literal: Now with defeats in the east and setbacks in the west, the trend of affairs is clear.
translations.idiomatic: With defeats in the east and setbacks in the west, the trend of affairs is plain.

sentences.zh: 不如早擇所依。」

translations.literal: It is better to choose early whom to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: We had better choose early whom to serve."

sentences.zh: 鑒然其言，相率歸太祖。

translations.literal: Jian approved his words, and together they led their men to submit to the founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian agreed, and together they led their men to submit to the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 隸李文忠，從赴池州，力戰，流矢中右股，拔去，戰自若。

translations.literal: He served under Li Wenzhong, followed him to Chizhou, fought fiercely, was struck by a stray arrow in the right thigh, pulled it out, and fought as before.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Li Wenzhong and followed him to Chizhou, fighting fiercely; a stray arrow struck his right thigh, but he pulled it out and fought on as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 取於潛、昌化，克嚴州，皆預，進萬戶。

translations.literal: In taking Yuqian and Changhua and capturing Yanzhou he took part in all, and was promoted to myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Yuqian and Changhua and the reduction of Yanzhou, and was promoted to myriarch.

sentences.zh: 苗帥楊完者軍烏龍嶺，德請曰：「此可襲而取也。」

translations.literal: When Miao commander Yang Wanzhe encamped at Wulong Ridge, De requested and said: "This can be taken by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao commander Yang Wanzhe encamped at Wulong Ridge, De said, "This position can be taken by surprise."

sentences.zh: 文忠問故。

translations.literal: Wenzhong asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong asked why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「乘高覘之，其部曲徙舉不安而聲囂。」

translations.literal: He replied: "From high ground I observed them; their subordinates moved restlessly and uneasily and their voices were clamorous."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "From the heights I watched them—their troops were restless and their voices loud with alarm."

sentences.zh: 文忠曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 即襲完者，覆其營。

translations.literal: He immediately raided Wanzhe and overthrew his camp.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately raided Wanzhe and overran his camp.

sentences.zh: 取蘭溪，克諸暨，攻紹興，皆先登陷陣，傷右臂不顧。

translations.literal: In taking Lanxi, capturing Zhuji, and attacking Shaoxing, he was always first to scale the walls and break the ranks, wounded in the right arm yet heedless.
translations.idiomatic: At Lanxi, Zhuji, and Shaoxing he was always first over the walls and into the enemy ranks, ignoring wounds to his right arm.

sentences.zh: 文忠嘆曰：「將士人人如此，何戰不捷哉。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong sighed and said: "If officers and soldiers were all like this, what battle would not be victorious?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong exclaimed, "If every officer and soldier were like this, what battle could we lose?"

sentences.zh: 蔣英、賀仁德之叛，浙東大震。

translations.literal: When Jiang Ying and He Rende rebelled, eastern Zhejiang was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ying and He Rende rebelled, eastern Zhejiang was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 從文忠定金華，又從攻處州。

translations.literal: He followed Wenzhong in settling Jinhua and again followed in attacking Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wenzhong in pacifying Jinhua and again in the attack on Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇仁德於劉山，戈中右股，德引刀斷戈，追擊之。

translations.literal: He met Rende at Liu Mountain; a halberd struck his right thigh, and De drew his blade and severed the halberd, then pursued and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: He met Rende at Liu Mountain; a halberd struck his right thigh, but De drew his sword, severed the shaft, and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 仁德再戰，再敗走，遂為其下所殺。

translations.literal: Rende fought again, was again defeated and fled, and was thereupon killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Rende fought again, was defeated again and fled, and was then killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 德還師守嚴。

translations.literal: De returned with the army to guard Yan.
translations.idiomatic: De returned with the army to garrison Yan.

sentences.zh: 後二年，定官制，改管軍百戶。

translations.literal: Two years later the official system was fixed and he was changed to Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when the official system was established, he was made Company Commander.

sentences.zh: 從文忠破張士誠兵於諸暨，與諸將援浦城，所過山寨皆下。

translations.literal: He followed Wenzhong in defeating Zhang Shicheng's troops at Zhuji, and with the generals relieved Pucheng; every mountain stockade they passed submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wenzhong in defeating Zhang Shicheng's forces at Zhuji and, with other generals, relieved Pucheng; every mountain stockade along the way submitted.

sentences.zh: 復從文忠下建、延、汀三州，悉定閩溪諸寨。

translations.literal: Again he followed Wenzhong in reducing the three prefectures Jian, Yan, and Ting, and altogether pacified the stockades of Minxi.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Wenzhong in reducing Jian, Yan, and Ting and pacified all the stockades of Minxi.

sentences.zh: 進管軍千戶，移守衢，予世襲。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Battalion Commander, transferred to guard Qu, and granted hereditary tenure.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Battalion Commander, transferred to garrison Qu, and granted a hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 最後從靖海侯吳禎巡海上。

translations.literal: Finally he followed Marquis of Jinghai Wu Zhen in patrolling the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he accompanied the Marquis of Jinghai, Wu Zhen, on coastal patrols.

sentences.zh: 禎以德可任，令守平陽。

translations.literal: Zhen, because De was capable, ordered him to guard Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, judging De trustworthy, appointed him to guard Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 在任八年，致仕。

translations.literal: He was in office eight years and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he retired.

sentences.zh: 及征雲南，帝以德宿將，命與諸大帥偕行。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was campaigned against, the emperor, because De was a veteran general, ordered him to go together with the great commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Yunnan was launched, the emperor, recognizing De as a veteran, ordered him to march with the chief commanders.

sentences.zh: 張鑒，又名明鑒，淮西人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, also named Mingjian, was a man of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, also known as Mingjian, came from Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 既歸太祖，每攻伐必與德俱，先德卒。

translations.literal: After submitting to the founding emperor, in every attack he was always together with De; he died before De.
translations.idiomatic: After joining the founding emperor, he fought in every campaign alongside De and died before him.

sentences.zh: 官至江淮行樞密院副使。

translations.literal: His office reached Vice Commissioner of the Jianghuai Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Commissioner of the Jianghuai Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 蔡遷，不詳其鄉里，元末從芝麻李據徐州。

translations.literal: Cai Qian, whose native place is not recorded in detail, at the end of Yuan followed Sesame Li in holding Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qian, whose home district is not recorded, followed Sesame Li in holding Xuzhou at the end of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 李敗，歸太祖，為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Li was defeated, he submitted to the founding emperor and became a vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Li was defeated, he submitted to the founding emperor and served as a vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，下採石，克太平，取溧水，破蠻子海牙水寨及陳埜先，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, took Caishi, captured Taiping, seized Lishui, and broke Manzi Haiya's river stockade and Chen Youxian—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with the army, took Caishi, captured Taiping, seized Lishui, and broke Manzi Haiya's river stockade and Chen Youxian's forces, earning merit in each action.

sentences.zh: 定集慶，授千戶。

translations.literal: When Jiqing was settled he was appointed chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Jiqing he was appointed chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取廣德、寧國，遷萬戶。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Guangde and Ningguo and was transferred to myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in taking Guangde and Ningguo and was promoted to myriarch.

sentences.zh: 進攻常州，獲黃元帥，遂為都先鋒。

translations.literal: In advancing to attack Changzhou he captured Marshal Huang and thereupon became Chief Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Changzhou he captured Marshal Huang and was made Chief Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從征馬馱沙，克池州，攻樅陽，從征衢、婺二州，授帳前左翼元帥。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns at Matuosha, captured Chizhou, attacked Zongyang, followed campaigns in the two prefectures Qu and Wu, and was appointed Left Vanguard Marshal before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned at Matuosha, captured Chizhou, attacked Zongyang, and campaigned in Qu and Wu, and was appointed Left Vanguard Marshal of the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 敗陳友諒於龍江，進復太平，取安慶水寨，收九江，敗友諒八陣指揮於瑞昌，遂克南昌。

translations.literal: He defeated Chen Youliang at Longjiang, advanced to recover Taiping, took Anqing's river stockade, recovered Jiujiang, defeated Youliang's Eight-Array Commander at Ruichang, and thereupon captured Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Chen Youliang at Longjiang, recovered Taiping, seized Anqing's river stockade, took Jiujiang, routed Youliang's Eight-Array Commander at Ruichang, and captured Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，攻合肥，戰鄱陽。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Anfeng, attacked Hefei, and fought at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Anfeng, attacked Hefei, and fought at Poyang.

sentences.zh: 從征武昌，進指揮同知。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Wuchang and was promoted to Associate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Wuchang and was promoted to Associate Commander.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春討平鄧克明余黨，進攻贛州。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in suppressing Deng Keming's remaining faction and advanced to attack Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun in suppressing Deng Keming's remaining followers and advanced on Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 取南安、南雄諸郡，還兵追饒鼎臣於茶陵，遷龍驤衛同知。

translations.literal: He took the prefectures Nan'an and Nanxiong and others, returned troops to pursue Rao Dingchen at Chaling, and was transferred to Associate Commander of the Dragon Soaring Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He took Nan'an, Nanxiong, and other prefectures, turned back to pursue Rao Dingchen at Chaling, and was transferred to Associate Commander of the Dragon Soaring Guard.

sentences.zh: 從徐達克高郵，破馬港，授武德衛指揮使，守淮安，移守黃州。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in capturing Gaoyou and breaking Magang, was appointed Commander of the Wude Guard, guarded Huai'an, and was transferred to guard Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in capturing Gaoyou and breaking Magang, was appointed Commander of the Wude Guard, garrisoned Huai'an, and was later transferred to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 從下湘潭、辰、全、道、永諸州，轉荊州衛指揮。

translations.literal: He followed in reducing Xiangtan and the prefectures Chen, Quan, Dao, and Yong, and was transferred to Commander of the Jingzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He helped reduce Xiangtan and the prefectures Chen, Quan, Dao, and Yong, and was transferred to Commander of the Jingzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 進克廣西，遷廣西行省參政，兼靖江王相，討平諸叛蠻。

translations.literal: He advanced to capture Guangxi, was transferred to Guangxi Branch Secretariat Administrator, concurrently Prince of Jingjiang's Chancellor, and suppressed the various rebellious Miao.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced into Guangxi, was made Administrator of the Guangxi Branch Secretariat and concurrently Chancellor to the Prince of Jingjiang, and suppressed the rebellious tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年九月卒，詔歸葬京師，贈安遠侯，諡武襄。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Hongwu he died; an edict ordered his burial returned to the capital; he was posthumously granted Marquis of Anyuan with the posthumous title Martial Support.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Hongwu year 3; an edict ordered his remains returned to the capital for burial; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyuan with the temple name Martial Support.

sentences.zh: 遷為將十五年，未嘗獨任，多從諸將征討。

translations.literal: Qian was a general for fifteen years and never held independent command, mostly following the generals on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Qian served as a general for fifteen years, never holding independent command but fighting under senior commanders on campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 身經數十戰，輒奮勇突出，橫刀左右擊，敵皆披靡，不敢近。

translations.literal: His body passed through several tens of battles; he would always burst forth bravely, sweep his blade left and right, and the enemy all collapsed and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Through dozens of battles he would burst forward fearlessly, sweeping his blade left and right until the enemy broke and dared not come near.

sentences.zh: 既還，金瘡滿體，人視之不可堪。

translations.literal: When he returned, golden sores covered his body; others looking at him could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from battle, his body was covered with scars so grievous that onlookers could scarcely bear to look.

sentences.zh: 而遷略不為意，為太祖所愛重。

translations.literal: Yet Qian paid no heed and was loved and esteemed by the founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qian thought nothing of them and was held in deep affection by the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 及卒，尤痛惜之，親制文祭焉。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor especially grieved for him and personally composed a text to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor grieved deeply and personally composed a funeral elegy.

sentences.zh: 附 陳文

translations.literal: Appended: Chen Wen
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Chen Wen

sentences.zh: 合肥陳文者，南北征伐，累立戰功，亦遷亞也。

translations.literal: Chen Wen of Hefei, in northern and southern campaigns, repeatedly established military achievements and was also second to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen of Hefei, who campaigned north and south and won repeated victories, ranked second only to Qian.

sentences.zh: 文少孤，奉母至孝，元季挈家歸太祖，積官都督僉事。

translations.literal: Wen was orphaned young, served his mother with utmost filial piety, at the end of Yuan brought his family to submit to the founding emperor, and accumulated office to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen lost his father young and served his mother with exemplary filial devotion; at the end of the Yuan he brought his family to join the founding emperor and rose to Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，追封東海侯，諡孝勇。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Donghai with the posthumous title Filial Valor.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Donghai with the temple name Filial Valor.

sentences.zh: 明臣得諡孝者，文一人而已。

translations.literal: Among Ming ministers who received the posthumous title Filial, Wen alone was such.
translations.idiomatic: Among Ming ministers granted the posthumous element "Filial" in their temple names, Wen alone received it.

sentences.zh: 王銘，字子敬，和州人。

translations.literal: Wang Ming, styled Zijing, was a man of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ming, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 初隸元帥俞通海麾下，從攻蠻子海牙於採石。

translations.literal: At first he served under Marshal Yu Tonghai and followed in attacking Manzi Haiya at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Marshal Yu Tonghai and took part in the attack on Manzi Haiya at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 以銘驍勇，選充奇兵。

translations.literal: Because Ming was fierce and brave, he was selected to serve in the elite assault corps.
translations.idiomatic: For his ferocity and courage, Ming was chosen for the elite shock troops.

sentences.zh: 戰方合，帥敢死士大噪突之，拔其水寨。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, he led dare-to-die warriors in a great clamor and charged; they took the enemy's water fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the fight was joined, he led dare-to-die warriors in a thunderous charge and captured the enemy's river fort.

sentences.zh: 自是數有功。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly won achievement.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he won repeated distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 與吳軍戰太湖，流矢中右臂，引佩刀出其鏃，復戰。

translations.literal: Fighting Wu forces at Taihu Lake, a stray arrow struck his right arm; he drew his belt dagger to extract the arrowhead and returned to battle.
translations.idiomatic: In battle with Wu forces on Taihu Lake, a stray arrow struck his right arm; he drew his belt dagger, pulled out the arrowhead, and went back to the fight.

sentences.zh: 通海勞之。

translations.literal: Tonghai commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai rewarded him for his service.

sentences.zh: 復拔通州之黃橋、鵝項諸寨。

translations.literal: Again he captured the stockades of Huangqiao and Exiang in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again captured the Huangqiao and Exiang stockades in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 賜白金文綺。

translations.literal: He was granted white gold and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: He received gifts of white gold and patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 龍灣之戰，逐北至採石，銘獨突敵陣。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Longwan, pursuing the enemy north to Caishi, Ming alone charged into the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Longwan, as the pursuit pressed north to Caishi, Ming alone burst into the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 敵兵攢槊刺銘，傷頰。

translations.literal: Enemy soldiers thrust their spears at Ming and wounded his cheek.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy soldiers thrust their spears at Ming and wounded his cheek.

sentences.zh: 銘三出三入，所殺傷過當。

translations.literal: Ming went out and in three times; those he killed and wounded exceeded the equivalent.
translations.idiomatic: Ming charged out and back three times, and the enemy he killed and wounded far exceeded his own losses.

sentences.zh: 賜文綺銀碗，選充宿衛。

translations.literal: He was granted patterned silks and a silver bowl and was selected for the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He received patterned silks and a silver bowl and was chosen for the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 從取江州，戰康郎山及涇江口，復克英山諸寨，擢管軍百戶。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Jiangzhou, fought at Kanglang Mountain and Jingjiang Estuary, again captured the stockades of Yingshan, and was promoted to company commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the capture of Jiangzhou, fought at Kanglang Mountain and the Jingjiang estuary, took the Yingshan stockades, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 從副將軍常遇春戰湖州之升山。

translations.literal: He followed Vice General Chang Yuchun in battle at Shengshan in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Vice General Chang Yuchun in the battle at Shengshan in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 再戰舊館，已，又戰烏鎮。

translations.literal: He fought again at Jiuguan; soon after, he fought again at Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Jiuguan; soon after, he fought again at Wuzhen.

sentences.zh: 前後數十戰，功多，命守松江。

translations.literal: In several dozen battles before and after, his achievements were many, and he was ordered to garrison Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In several dozen battles before and after, his achievements were many, and he was ordered to garrison Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 移太倉，捕斬倭寇千餘人，再賜金幣。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taicang, he captured and beheaded more than a thousand Japanese pirates and was again granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Taicang, he captured and beheaded more than a thousand Japanese pirates and was again granted gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，都試百戶諸善用槍者，率莫能與銘抗。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 4, when all company commanders skilled with the spear were tested throughout, generally none could match Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 4, when all company commanders skilled with the spear were tested throughout, generally none could match Ming.

sentences.zh: 累官至長淮衛指揮僉事，移守溫州。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he reached Vice Commander of the Changhuai Guard and was transferred to garrison Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to Vice Commander of the Changhuai Guard and was transferred to garrison Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣所領鎮，外控島夷，城池樓櫓仍陋襲簡，非獨不足壯國威，猝有風潮之變，捍禦無所，勢須改為。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying: "The garrison I command faces the island barbarians across the sea; its walls, city, and towers remain crude and antiquated. This is not merely insufficient to display the nation's majesty—if a sudden storm or tide should change, there would be nowhere to defend; the situation demands that they be rebuilt."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial, saying, "The fortress I command faces the island barbarians across the sea, yet its walls and towers remain crude and outmoded. That alone is not enough to display the nation's majesty; if wind or tide should suddenly turn, there would be nowhere to make a stand—the situation demands that they be rebuilt."

sentences.zh: 帝報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 於是繕城浚濠，悉倍於舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired the walls and dredged the moat, all doubling the old scale.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he repaired the walls and dredged the moat, doubling everything that had stood before.

sentences.zh: 加築外垣，起海神山屬郭公山，首尾二千余丈，宏敞壯麗，屹然東浙巨鎮。

translations.literal: An outer rampart was added, running from Mount Haishan through to Mount Guogong, more than two thousand zhang from end to end—spacious, splendid, and magnificent, standing firm as the great fortress of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He added an outer wall running from Mount Haishan to Mount Guogong, more than two thousand zhang from end to end—spacious, splendid, and magnificent, a towering stronghold of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之，予世襲。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly commended him and granted hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly commended him and granted hereditary succession of his post.

sentences.zh: 銘嘗請告暫還和州。

translations.literal: Ming once requested leave to return temporarily to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ming once asked leave to return briefly to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 溫士女遮道送迎。

translations.literal: Men and women of Wenzhou blocked the road to see him off and welcome him back.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of Wenzhou lined the road to see him off and welcome him home.

sentences.zh: 長吏皆相顧嘆曰：「吾屬為天子牧民，民視吾屬去來漠然，愧王指揮多矣。」

translations.literal: The senior officials all looked at one another and sighed, saying: "We are shepherds of the people for the Son of Heaven, yet the people regard our comings and goings with indifference—we fall far short of Commander Wang."
translations.idiomatic: The senior officials looked at one another and sighed, "We are shepherds of the people for the Son of Heaven, yet the people take our comings and goings with indifference—we are shamed beside Commander Wang."

sentences.zh: 歷右軍都督僉事，二十六年坐藍玉黨死。

translations.literal: He rose through Vice Commissioner of the Right Army Directorate; in year twenty-six he was executed as a member of Lan Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Commissioner of the Right Army Directorate; in Hongwu year 26 he was executed in the Lan Yu faction case.

sentences.zh: 寧正，字正卿，壽州人。

translations.literal: Ning Zheng, styled Zhengqing, was a man of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Zheng, whose courtesy name was Zhengqing, came from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼為韋德成養子，冒韋姓。

translations.literal: In youth he became the adopted son of Wei Decheng and took the Wei surname.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he became the adopted son of Wei Decheng and took the Wei surname.

sentences.zh: 元末隨德成來歸，從渡江。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he followed Decheng in submission and crossed the Yangzi with the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he followed Decheng in submission and crossed the Yangzi with the army.

sentences.zh: 德成戰歿宣州，以正領其眾。

translations.literal: When Decheng died in battle at Xuanzhou, Zheng took command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Decheng fell in battle at Xuanzhou, Zheng took command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 積功授鳳翔衛指揮副使。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was appointed Associate Commander of the Fengxiang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he was appointed Associate Commander of the Fengxiang Guard.

sentences.zh: 從定中原，入元都，招降元將士八千餘人。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of the Central Plain, he entered the Yuan capital and induced more than eight thousand Yuan officers and soldiers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of the Central Plain, entered the Yuan capital, and induced more than eight thousand Yuan officers and soldiers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 傅友德自真定略平定州，以正守真定。

translations.literal: Fu Youde advanced from Zhending to take Dingzhou, and Zheng was left to guard Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Youde advanced from Zhending to take Dingzhou, Zheng was left to hold Zhending.

sentences.zh: 已，從大軍取陝西。

translations.literal: Soon after, he followed the main army in taking Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he followed the main army in the conquest of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 馮勝克臨洮，留正守之。

translations.literal: Feng Sheng captured Lintao and left Zheng to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Sheng captured Lintao, he left Zheng to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 大軍圍慶陽，正駐邠州，絕敵聲援。

translations.literal: When the main army besieged Qingyang, Zheng encamped at Binzhou and cut off the enemy's communications and reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army besieged Qingyang, Zheng encamped at Binzhou and severed the enemy's lines of communication and relief.

sentences.zh: 慶陽下，還守臨洮。

translations.literal: When Qingyang fell, he returned to garrison Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyang fell, he returned to garrison Lintao.

sentences.zh: 從鄧愈破定西，克河州。

translations.literal: He followed Deng Yu in breaking Dingxi and capturing Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Deng Yu in breaking Dingxi and capturing Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，授河州衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 3 he was appointed Commander of the Hezhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he was appointed Commander of the Hezhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 上言：「西民轉粟餉軍甚勞，而茶布可易粟。

translations.literal: He reported to the throne: "The western people labor greatly transporting grain to supply the army, yet tea and cloth can be exchanged for grain.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the throne, "The people of the west labor greatly hauling grain to supply the army, yet tea and cloth can be traded for grain.

sentences.zh: 請以茶布給軍，令自相貿易，省挽運之苦。」

translations.literal: I ask that tea and cloth be issued to the troops and they be allowed to trade among themselves, sparing the hardship of haulage."
translations.idiomatic: May tea and cloth be issued to the troops and they be allowed to trade among themselves, sparing the hardship of transport by cart and shoulder."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict accepted the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 正初至衛，城邑空虛，勤於勞徠。

translations.literal: When Zheng first arrived at the guard, the city and towns were empty; he worked diligently to settle and attract people.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng first arrived at the guard, the city and towns lay empty; he worked tirelessly to settle and attract people.

sentences.zh: 不數年，河州遂為樂土。

translations.literal: Within a few years Hezhou became a land of contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Hezhou became a land of peace and plenty.

sentences.zh: 璽書嘉勞，始復甯姓。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended and rewarded him, and he at last restored the Ning surname.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter commended and rewarded him, and he at last restored the Ning surname.

sentences.zh: 兼領寧夏衛事。

translations.literal: He also took charge of the Ningxia Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also took charge of the Ningxia Guard.

sentences.zh: 修築漢、唐舊渠，引河水溉田，開屯數萬頃，兵食饒足。

translations.literal: He repaired the old Han and Tang canals, drew river water to irrigate fields, opened up tens of thousands of qing of military colonies, and military provisions became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the old Han and Tang canals, drew river water to irrigate the fields, opened tens of thousands of qing of military colonies, and the troops' provisions grew ample.

sentences.zh: 十三年從沐英北征，擒元平章脫火赤、知院愛足，取全寧四部。

translations.literal: In year thirteen he followed Mu Ying on the northern expedition, captured the Yuan Pacification Commissioner Tuohuochi and Court Commissioner Aizu, and took the four divisions of Quanning.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 13 he followed Mu Ying on the northern campaign, captured the Yuan Pacification Commissioner Tuohuochi and Court Commissioner Aizu, and took the four divisions of Quanning.

sentences.zh: 十五年遷四川都指揮使，討平松、茂諸州。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Sichuan and campaigned to pacify Song, Mao, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 15 he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Sichuan and campaigned to pacify Song, Mao, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 雲南初定，命正與馮誠共守之。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was first pacified, he was ordered together with Feng Cheng to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan was first pacified, he was ordered to garrison it together with Feng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 思倫發作亂，正破之於摩沙勒寨，斬首千五百。

translations.literal: When Si Lunfa revolted, Zheng defeated him at the Moshaled stockade and took fifteen hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: When Si Lunfa rebelled, Zheng defeated him at the Moshaled stockade and took fifteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 已，敵眾大集，圍定邊。

translations.literal: Soon after, the enemy massed in great numbers and besieged Dingbian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the enemy gathered in force and besieged Dingbian.

sentences.zh: 沐英分兵三隊，正將左軍，鏖戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Mu Ying divided his forces into three columns; Zheng commanded the left army; after fierce fighting they routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ying divided his forces into three columns; Zheng commanded the left wing; after a bitter fight they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 語在《英傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Ying."
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the biography of Ying [Mu Ying].

sentences.zh: 土酋阿資叛，復從英討降之。

translations.literal: The native chieftain A Zi rebelled; Zheng again followed Ying to campaign and induce his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the native chieftain A Zi rebelled, Zheng again followed Ying to campaign and bring about his surrender.

sentences.zh: 英卒，詔授正左都督代鎮。

translations.literal: When Ying died, an edict appointed Zheng Left Chief Commander to replace him in commanding the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, an edict appointed Zheng Left Chief Commander to replace him in command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 已，覆命為平羌將軍，總川、陝兵討平階、文叛寇張者。

translations.literal: Soon after, he received renewed orders as General Pacifying the Qiang, commanding Sichuan and Shaanxi troops to suppress and pacify the rebel bandit Zhang Zhe of Jie and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he received renewed orders as General Pacifying the Qiang, commanding Sichuan and Shaanxi troops to suppress the rebel Zhang Zhe of Jie and Wen.

sentences.zh: 二十八年從秦王討平洮州番，還京。

translations.literal: In year twenty-eight he followed the Prince of Qin in suppressing the Tibetan tribes of Taozhou and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 28 he followed the Prince of Qin in suppressing the Tibetan tribes of Taozhou and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died.

sentences.zh: 附 袁義

translations.literal: Appended: Yuan Yi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Yuan Yi

sentences.zh: 又袁義，廬江人，本張姓，德勝族弟也。

translations.literal: Also Yuan Yi, a man of Lujiang; originally surnamed Zhang and a clansman younger brother of Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yuan Yi, a man of Lujiang; originally surnamed Zhang, he was a younger clansman of Desheng.

sentences.zh: 初為雙刀趙總管，守安慶，敗趙同僉、丁普郎於沙子港。

translations.literal: At first he served as commander under Two-Swords Zhao, garrisoned Anqing, and defeated Zhao Tongqian and Ding Pulang at Shazigang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Two-Swords Zhao as a commander, garrisoned Anqing, and defeated Zhao Tongqian and Ding Pulang at Shazigang.

sentences.zh: 左君弼招之，弗從。

translations.literal: Zuo Junbi recruited him, but he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Junbi tried to recruit him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 德勝戰死，始來附。

translations.literal: When Desheng died in battle, he at last came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Desheng fell in battle, he at last came over to the Ming side.

sentences.zh: 為帳前親軍元帥，賜姓名。

translations.literal: He was made Personal Guard Marshal before the commander's tent and was granted a surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: He was made marshal of the personal guard before the commander's tent and was granted a surname and personal name.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，積功為興武衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He followed on several campaigns; through accumulated merit he became Vice Commander of the Xingwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed on several campaigns and, through accumulated merit, rose to Vice Commander of the Xingwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍北征，敗元平章俺普達等於通州，走賀宗哲、詹同於澤、潞，功最。

translations.literal: Following the Great General on the northern expedition, he defeated the Yuan Pacification Commissioner An Puda and others at Tongzhou, drove He Zongzhe and Zhan Tong through Ze and Lu, and his achievements ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Great General on the northern expedition, he defeated the Yuan Pacification Commissioner An Puda and others at Tongzhou, drove He Zongzhe and Zhan Tong through Ze and Lu, and his achievements ranked first.

sentences.zh: 復從定陝西，敗元豫王兵。

translations.literal: Again he followed in pacifying Shaanxi and defeated the troops of the Yuan Prince of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in the pacification of Shaanxi and defeated the troops of the Yuan Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 與諸將合攻慶陽。

translations.literal: Together with the other generals he jointly attacked Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the other generals he joined in the attack on Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 張良臣兵驟薄義營，義堅壁不為動，俟其懈，力擊破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangchen's troops suddenly pressed close to Yi's camp; Yi held the walls firm and did not stir, waited until they slackened, then struck with force and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liangchen's troops suddenly pressed close to Yi's camp, Yi held firm behind his walls and did not stir; when they slackened, he struck with force and broke them.

sentences.zh: 走擴廓軍於定西，南取興元。

translations.literal: He drove Köke Temür's army at Dingxi and took Xingyuan to the south.
translations.idiomatic: He drove Köke Temür's army from Dingxi and took Xingyuan to the south.

sentences.zh: 進本衛同知，調羽林衛，移鎮遼東。

translations.literal: Promoted to Associate Commander of his guard, transferred to the Yulin Guard, and moved to garrison Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Associate Commander of his guard, transferred to the Yulin Guard, and posted to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 金興旺

translations.literal: Jin Xingwang
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xingwang

sentences.zh: 明年攻臨洮，移興旺守鳳翔，轉軍餉。

translations.literal: The next year, when Lintao was attacked, Xingwang was transferred to guard Fengxiang and transport military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, during the attack on Lintao, Xingwang was transferred to guard Fengxiang and transport military supplies.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賀宗哲攻鳳翔，興旺與知府周煥嬰城守。

translations.literal: Before long He Zongzhe attacked Fengxiang; Xingwang and Prefect Zhou Huan sealed the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long He Zongzhe attacked Fengxiang; Xingwang and Prefect Zhou Huan sealed the city and held it fast.

sentences.zh: 敵編荊為大箕，形如半舫。

translations.literal: The enemy wove thorns into great wicker shields shaped like half a boat.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy wove thorns into great wicker shields shaped like half a boat.

sentences.zh: 每箕五人，負之攻城，矢石不能入。

translations.literal: Five men per shield carried them to assault the walls; arrows and stones could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Five men to each shield carried them against the walls; arrows and stones could not penetrate.

sentences.zh: 投藁焚之，輒揚起。

translations.literal: They cast straw to burn them, but the flames always flared up.
translations.idiomatic: They cast straw to set them ablaze, but the flames always flared up uselessly.

sentences.zh: 乃置鉤藁中，擲著其隙，火遂熾，敵棄箕走。

translations.literal: Then they placed hooks in the straw, threw them into the gaps, and the fire blazed; the enemy abandoned the shields and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then they hid hooks in the straw, threw them into the gaps, and the fire caught fast; the enemy abandoned the shields and fled.

sentences.zh: 復為地道薄城。

translations.literal: Again they dug a tunnel to approach the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Again they dug a tunnel to approach the wall.

sentences.zh: 城中以矛迎刺，敵死甚眾，而攻不已。

translations.literal: Inside the city they met them with spears; many of the enemy died, yet the assault did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city the defenders met them with spears; many of the enemy fell, yet the assault did not let up.

sentences.zh: 興旺與煥謀曰：「彼謂我援師不至，必不敢出。

translations.literal: Xingwang and Huan plotted together, saying: "They will think our relief troops have not arrived and surely will not dare sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang and Huan plotted together, saying, "They will think our relief has not arrived and surely will not dare sally out.

sentences.zh: 乘其不意擊之，可敗也。」

translations.literal: If we strike when they do not expect it, we can defeat them."
translations.idiomatic: If we strike when they do not expect it, we can defeat them."

sentences.zh: 潛出西北門，奮戰，敵少卻。

translations.literal: Stealthily they went out the northwest gate, fought fiercely, and the enemy fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Stealthily they went out the northwest gate, fought fiercely, and the enemy fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 會百戶王輅自臨洮收李思齊降卒東還，即以其眾入城共守。

translations.literal: It happened that Centurion Wang Luo, returning east from Lintao with Li Siqi's surrendered troops, entered the city with his men to join in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Centurion Wang Luo, returning east from Lintao with Li Siqi's surrendered troops, brought his men into the city to join in the defense.

sentences.zh: 敵拔營去。
