translations.literal: The enemy struck camp and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 眾欲追之，輅曰：「未敗而退，誘我也。」

translations.literal: The men wished to pursue, but Luo said: "To retreat without having been defeated is to lure us."
translations.idiomatic: The men wished to pursue, but Luo said, "To withdraw without having been defeated is to lure us."

sentences.zh: 遣騎偵之。

translations.literal: He sent horsemen to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: He sent horsemen to scout ahead.

sentences.zh: 至五里坡，伏果發。

translations.literal: At Wulipu the ambush sprang as expected.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulipu the ambush sprang as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 還師復圍城。

translations.literal: The enemy turned back and again besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy turned back and again besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲走。

translations.literal: The men debated fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: The men debated abandoning the city.

sentences.zh: 興旺叱曰：「天子以城畀我，寧可去耶！」

translations.literal: Xingwang rebuked them, saying: "The Son of Heaven entrusted this city to me—how could I abandon it!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang rebuked them, saying, "The Son of Heaven entrusted this city to me—how could I abandon it!"

sentences.zh: 以輅所將皆新附，慮生變，乃括城中貲畜積庭中，令曰：「敵少緩，當大犒新兵。」

translations.literal: Because the troops Luo commanded were all newly surrendered men, fearing mutiny, he gathered the city's wealth and livestock in the courtyard and ordered: "When the enemy slackens a little, we shall feast the new troops generously."
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops under Luo were all newly surrendered men and he feared mutiny, he gathered the city's wealth and livestock in the courtyard and ordered, "When the enemy slackens a little, we shall feast the new troops generously."

sentences.zh: 新兵喜，協力固守。

translations.literal: The new troops rejoiced and joined in holding the city with united effort.
translations.idiomatic: The new troops rejoiced and joined in the defense with one heart.

sentences.zh: 相持十五日，敵聞慶陽下，乃引去。

translations.literal: After holding out fifteen days, the enemy heard that Qingyang had fallen and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen days of stalemate, the enemy heard that Qingyang had fallen and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使以金綺勞興旺等。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy with gold and silks to reward Xingwang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy with gold and silks to reward Xingwang and the others.

sentences.zh: 明年，達入沔州，遣興旺與張龍由鳳翔入連雲棧，合攻興元。

translations.literal: The next year, when Da entered Mianzhou, he dispatched Xingwang and Zhang Long through Fengxiang into the Lianyun plank road to join in the attack on Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xu Da entered Mianzhou and dispatched Xingwang and Zhang Long through Fengxiang into the Lianyun plank road to join in the attack on Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 守將降，以興旺守之，擢大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: The defending general surrendered; Xingwang was put in charge of the city and promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general surrendered; Xingwang was left to hold the city and promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 蜀將吳友仁帥眾三萬寇興元，興旺悉城中兵三千禦敵。

translations.literal: The Shu general Wu Youren led thirty thousand men to raid Xingyuan; Xingwang mustered all three thousand troops in the city to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu general Wu Youren led thirty thousand men against Xingyuan; Xingwang mustered the city's entire force of three thousand to meet them.

sentences.zh: 面中流矢，拔矢復戰，斬數百人。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his face; he pulled it out and fought on again, killing several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Struck in the face by an arrow, he pulled it out and fought on, killing several hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵益眾，乃斂兵入城。

translations.literal: The enemy grew ever more numerous, so he drew his troops back into the city.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy swelled in number, he drew his troops back into the city.

sentences.zh: 友仁決濠填塹，為必克計。

translations.literal: Youren breached the moat and filled in the ditches, planning to take the city without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Youren breached the moat and filled in the ditches, determined to capture the city at all costs.

sentences.zh: 達聞之，令傅友德夜襲木槽關，攻斗山寨。

translations.literal: When Da heard of this, he ordered Fu Youde to raid Mucao Pass by night and attack Doushan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da heard of this, he ordered Fu Youde to strike Mucao Pass by night and attack Doushan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 人持十炬，連亙山上。

translations.literal: Each man carried ten torches, and they stretched in an unbroken line along the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Each man carried ten torches, and their fires stretched in an unbroken line along the ridgeline.

sentences.zh: 友仁驚遁。

translations.literal: Youren fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Youren fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 興旺出兵躡之，墜崖石死者無算。

translations.literal: Xingwang marched out in pursuit; those who fell from cliffs and rocks died beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang marched out in pursuit, and countless men perished falling from cliffs and rocks.

sentences.zh: 友仁自是氣奪。

translations.literal: From then on Youren's fighting spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Youren's fighting spirit was broken.

sentences.zh: 時興旺威鎮隴蜀。

translations.literal: At that time Xingwang's authority held sway over Long and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xingwang's authority held sway over Long and Shu.

sentences.zh: 附 費子賢

translations.literal: Appended: Fei Zixian
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Fei Zixian

sentences.zh: 而國初諸都督中，城守功，興旺外尤推費子賢。

translations.literal: Among the chief commanders at the founding of the dynasty, for achievements in holding cities, apart from Xingwang, Fei Zixian was especially esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the chief commanders of the dynasty's founding, for feats of holding cities, Fei Zixian was ranked next only to Xingwang.

sentences.zh: 子賢，亦不詳所始。

translations.literal: Zixian's origins, too, are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian's origins, too, are not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，為廣德翼元帥。

translations.literal: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi and served as deputy marshal of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi and served as deputy marshal of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 數有功。

translations.literal: He won merit on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in battle on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 取武康，又取安吉。

translations.literal: He took Wukang and then took Anji.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Wukang and then captured Anji.

sentences.zh: 築城守之，張士誠兵數來犯，輒敗去。

translations.literal: He built a city and held it; Zhang Shicheng's troops came to attack many times and were always beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified a city and held it; Zhang Shicheng's troops attacked repeatedly and were always driven off.

sentences.zh: 最後張左丞以兵八萬來攻，子賢所部僅三千人，而守甚固。

translations.literal: Finally Vice Minister Zhang came to attack with eighty thousand men; Zixian's force numbered only three thousand, yet the defense was very firm.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Vice Minister Zhang attacked with eighty thousand men; Zixian had only three thousand under his command, yet the defense held firm.

sentences.zh: 設車弩城上，射殺其梟將二人，敵乃解去。

translations.literal: He set ballista-carts on the walls and shot dead two of the enemy's leading generals, whereupon the foe withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted ballista-carts on the walls and killed two of the enemy's leading generals; the attackers then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功進指揮同知。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 取福建，克元都、定西，俱有功，授大都督府僉事，世指揮使。

translations.literal: In the conquest of Fujian and the capture of Yuandu and Dingxi he won merit on each occasion; he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission with a hereditary commandership.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Fujian and the capture of Yuandu and Dingxi he won merit throughout; he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission with a hereditary commandership.

sentences.zh: 花茂，巢縣人。

translations.literal: Hua Mao was a man of Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Mao came from Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 初從陳埜先，已而來歸。

translations.literal: At first he followed Chen Yexian, but later came over to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Chen Yexian, but later came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 從定江左，滅陳友諒。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the Jiangzuo region and the destruction of Chen Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the Jiangzuo region and in the destruction of Chen Youliang.

sentences.zh: 平中原、山西、陝西。

translations.literal: He helped pacify the Central Plain, Shanxi, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Central Plain, Shanxi, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 積功授武昌衛副千戶。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was appointed Deputy Chiliarch of the Wuchang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was appointed Deputy Chiliarch of the Wuchang Guard.

sentences.zh: 征西蜀。

translations.literal: He campaigned in western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in western Shu.

sentences.zh: 克瞿唐關，入重慶。

translations.literal: He captured Qutang Pass and entered Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Qutang Pass and entered Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 下左、右兩江及田州。

translations.literal: He subdued the Left and Right Rivers and Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued the Left and Right Rivers and Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 進神策衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commander of the Shence Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Commander of the Shence Guard.

sentences.zh: 調廣州左衛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Guangzhou Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Guangzhou Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 平陽春、清遠、英德、翁源、博羅諸山寨叛蠻及東莞、龍川諸縣亂民，進指揮同知。

translations.literal: He pacified rebel Miao in the stockades of Yangchun, Qingyuan, Yingde, Wengyuan, and Boluo, as well as the disorderly populace of Dongguan, Longchuan, and other counties, and was promoted to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified rebel tribes in the stockades of Yangchun, Qingyuan, Yingde, Wengyuan, and Boluo, as well as the unruly populace of Dongguan, Longchuan, and other counties, and was promoted to Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 平電白、歸善賊，再遷都指揮同知，世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandits of Dianbai and Guishan, was again promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief, and received a hereditary commandership.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the bandits of Dianbai and Guishan, was again promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief, and received a hereditary commandership.

sentences.zh: 數剿連州、廣西湖廣諸瑤賊。

translations.literal: He repeatedly suppressed Yao bandits in Lianzhou, Guangxi, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly suppressed Yao bandits in Lianzhou, Guangxi, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 上言：「廣東南邊大海，奸宄出沒。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying: "Guangdong's southern border faces the great sea, and treacherous evildoers come and go.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial, saying, "Guangdong's southern border faces the great sea, and treacherous evildoers come and go.

sentences.zh: 東莞、筍岡諸縣逋逃蜒戶，附居海島。

translations.literal: Fugitive boat-dwellers from Dongguan, Sun'gang, and other counties have settled on offshore islands.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive boat-dwellers from Dongguan, Sun'gang, and other counties have settled on offshore islands.

sentences.zh: 遇官軍則詭稱捕魚；

translations.literal: When they meet government troops they falsely claim to be fishing;
translations.idiomatic: When they meet government troops they falsely claim to be fishing;

sentences.zh: 遇番賊則同為寇盜。

translations.literal: when they meet foreign pirates they turn robber together.
translations.idiomatic: when they meet foreign pirates they turn robber together.

sentences.zh: 飄忽不常，難於訊詰。

translations.literal: They appear and vanish unpredictably and are hard to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: They appear and vanish unpredictably and are hard to investigate.

sentences.zh: 不若籍以為兵，庶便約束。」

translations.literal: It would be better to register them as soldiers so that they might more easily be kept under control."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to register them as soldiers so that they might more easily be kept under discipline."

sentences.zh: 又請設沿海依山廣海、碣石、神電等二十四衛所。

translations.literal: He also requested the establishment of twenty-four guards and posts along the coast, including Guanghai, Jieshi, and Shendian, built against the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested the establishment of twenty-four guards and posts along the coast, including Guanghai, Jieshi, and Shendian, built against the mountains.

sentences.zh: 築城浚池，收集海島隱料無籍等軍。

translations.literal: He proposed building walls, digging moats, and gathering hidden and unregistered troops from the offshore islands.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building walls, digging moats, and gathering hidden and unregistered troops from the offshore islands.

sentences.zh: 仍於山海要害地立堡屯軍，以備不虞。

translations.literal: He further proposed building forts and stationing troops at strategic points where mountains meet the sea, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed building forts and stationing troops at strategic points where mountains meet the sea, to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 久之卒，賜葬安德門。

translations.literal: After some time he died and was granted burial at Ande Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he died and was granted burial at Ande Gate.

sentences.zh: 長子榮襲職。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rong inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rong inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 次子英，果毅有父風，亦以軍功為廣東都指揮使，有聲永樂中。

translations.literal: His second son Ying was resolute and bold and had his father's bearing; he too rose through military merit to Commander-in-Chief of Guangdong and won renown during the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Ying was resolute and bold and had his father's bearing; he too rose through military merit to Commander-in-Chief of Guangdong and won renown during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 丁玉，初名國珍，河中人。

translations.literal: Ding Yu, originally named Guo Zhen, was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yu, originally named Guo Zhen, came from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 仕韓林兒為御史，才辨有時譽。

translations.literal: He served Han Lin'er as a censor and was talented in speech, winning contemporary repute.
translations.idiomatic: He served Han Lin'er as a censor and was gifted in debate, winning repute in his day.

sentences.zh: 呂珍破安豐，玉來歸。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhen captured Anfeng, Yu came over to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhen captured Anfeng, Yu came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 隨征彭蠡，為九江知府。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign at Poyang and was made Prefect of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign at Poyang and was made Prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 大兵還建康，彭澤山民叛，玉聚鄉兵討平之。

translations.literal: When the main army returned to Jiankang, the mountain people of Pengze rebelled; Yu gathered local militia and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned to Jiankang, the mountain people of Pengze rebelled; Yu gathered local militia and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其武略，命兼指揮，更名玉。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor commended his martial skill, ordered him to serve concurrently as a commander, and changed his name to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor commended his martial skill, ordered him to serve concurrently as a commander, and changed his name to Yu.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德克衡州，以指揮同知鎮其地。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde in capturing Hengzhou and was made Vice Commander to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Youde in capturing Hengzhou and was made Vice Commander to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 復調守永州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to guard Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to guard Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉有文武才，撫輯新附，威望甚著。

translations.literal: Yu possessed both civil and military talent; he soothed and gathered the newly surrendered, and his prestige was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Yu possessed both civil and military talent; he soothed and gathered the newly surrendered, and his prestige was very great.

sentences.zh: 郭雲，南陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Yun was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yun came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 長八尺余，狀貌魁偉。

translations.literal: He stood more than eight chi tall, with a towering and imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than eight chi tall, with a towering and imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 元季聚義兵保裕州泉白寨，累官湖廣行省平章政事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he gathered righteous troops to defend Quanbai Stockade in Yuzhou and rose through successive posts to Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he gathered righteous troops to defend Quanbai Stockade in Yuzhou and rose through successive posts to Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元主北奔，河南郡縣皆下，雲獨堅守。

translations.literal: When the Yuan ruler fled north, the prefectures and counties of Henan all submitted, but Yun alone held firm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan ruler fled north, the prefectures and counties of Henan all submitted, but Yun alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 大將軍徐達遣指揮曹諒圍之，雲出戰，被執。

translations.literal: The Grand General Xu Da dispatched Commander Cao Liang to besiege him; Yun sallied forth to fight and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Xu Da dispatched Commander Cao Liang to besiege him; Yun sallied forth to fight and was captured.

sentences.zh: 大將軍呵之跪。

translations.literal: The Grand General shouted at him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General shouted at him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 雲植立，嫚罵求死。

translations.literal: Yun stood upright, reviled them, and demanded death.
translations.idiomatic: Yun stood upright, reviled them, and demanded death.

sentences.zh: 脅以刃，不動。

translations.literal: Threatened with blades, he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Threatened with blades, he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 大將軍壯之，系送京師。

translations.literal: The Grand General admired his fortitude, bound him, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General admired his fortitude, bound him, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖奇其狀貌，釋之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor marveled at his appearance and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor marveled at his appearance and released him.

sentences.zh: 時帝方閱《漢書》，問識字否，對曰：「識。」

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was reading the Book of Han and asked whether he could read; he replied: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was reading the Book of Han and asked whether he could read; he replied, "I can."

sentences.zh: 因以書授之。

translations.literal: The emperor then handed him the book.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then handed him the book.

sentences.zh: 雲誦其書甚習。

translations.literal: Yun recited the book with great fluency.
translations.idiomatic: Yun recited from the book with great fluency.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，厚加賞賜，用為溧水知縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, rewarded him generously, and appointed him Magistrate of Lishui, where he won a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, rewarded him generously, and appointed him Magistrate of Lishui, where he won a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 帝益以為賢，特擢南陽衛指揮僉事，使還鄉收故部曲，就戍其地，凡數年卒。

translations.literal: The emperor came to esteem him all the more as worthy, specially promoted him to Vice Commander of the Nanyang Guard, and sent him home to gather his old followers and garrison the region; after several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to esteem him all the more, specially promoted him to Vice Commander of the Nanyang Guard, and sent him home to gather his old followers and garrison the region; after several years he died.

sentences.zh: 長子洪，年甫十三。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hong was just thirteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hong was just thirteen years old.

sentences.zh: 帝為下制曰：「雲出田間，倡義旗，保鄉曲，崎嶇累年，竭心所事。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict, saying: "Yun came from the fields, raised the banner of righteousness, and protected his home community; through years of hardship he devoted his heart to what he served.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict, saying, "Yun came from the fields, raised the banner of righteousness, and protected his home community; through years of hardship he devoted his heart to what he served.

sentences.zh: 王師北伐，人神響應。

translations.literal: When the royal army marched north, men and spirits responded alike.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army marched north, men and spirits responded alike.

sentences.zh: 而雲數戰不屈，勢窮援絕，終無異志。

translations.literal: Yet Yun fought many battles without yielding; when his strength was exhausted and aid cut off, he never wavered in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yun fought many battles without yielding; when his strength was exhausted and aid cut off, he never wavered in resolve.

sentences.zh: 朕嘉其節概。

translations.literal: We commend his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: We commend his fortitude.

sentences.zh: 試之有司，則閭閻頌德；

translations.literal: When tested by the officials, the common people praised his virtue;
translations.idiomatic: When tested by the officials, the common people praised his virtue;

sentences.zh: 俾鎮故鄉，則軍民樂業。

translations.literal: when posted to guard his homeland, soldiers and civilians lived contentedly.
translations.idiomatic: when posted to guard his homeland, soldiers and civilians lived contentedly.

sentences.zh: 雖無汗馬之勛，倒戈之效，治績克著，忠義凜然。

translations.literal: Although he won no distinction from sweat-stained horses nor from turning weapons in battle, his administrative achievements were outstanding and his loyalty and integrity stood radiant.
translations.idiomatic: Although he won no distinction from sweat-stained horses nor from turning weapons in battle, his administrative achievements were outstanding and his loyalty and integrity stood radiant.

sentences.zh: 子洪可入開國功臣列，授宣武將軍、飛熊衛親軍指揮使司僉事，世襲。」

translations.literal: His son Hong may enter the ranks of the founding meritocrats; let him be appointed General of Propagation of Might and Vice Commander of the Feixiong Guard Personal Army Command, with hereditary succession."
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong may enter the ranks of the founding meritocrats; let him be appointed General of Propagation of Might and Vice Commander of the Feixiong Guard Personal Army Command, with hereditary succession."

sentences.zh: 其同時以降將予世職者有王溥。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Wang Pu, among the surrendered generals granted hereditary posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Wang Pu, among the surrendered generals granted hereditary posts.

sentences.zh: 附 王溥

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Pu
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang Pu

sentences.zh: 初，溥未仕時，奉母葉氏避兵貴溪。

translations.literal: At first, before Pu had taken office, he escorted his mother, Lady Ye, to Guixi to escape the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before Pu had taken office, he escorted his mother, Lady Ye, to Guixi to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 遇亂，與母相失，凡十八年。

translations.literal: In the disorder he was separated from his mother—for eighteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorder he was separated from his mother—for eighteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 嘗夢母若告以所在，至是從容言於帝，請歸省墳墓。

translations.literal: He once dreamed that his mother seemed to tell him where she was; at this time he spoke calmly to the emperor and asked leave to return home and visit the graves.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that his mother seemed to tell him where she was; at this time he spoke calmly to the emperor and asked leave to return home and visit the graves.

sentences.zh: 許之，且命禮官具祭物。

translations.literal: The emperor granted permission and ordered the ritual officials to prepare offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted permission and ordered the ritual officials to prepare offerings.

sentences.zh: 溥率士卒之貴溪，求不得，晝夜號泣。

translations.literal: Pu led his soldiers to Guixi but could not find her and wept day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Pu led his soldiers to Guixi but could not find her and wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 居人吳海言：「夫人為賊逼，投井中死矣。」

translations.literal: A local man named Wu Hai said: "Your lady was forced by bandits and died by throwing herself into a well."
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Wu Hai said, "Your lady was forced by bandits and died by throwing herself into a well."

sentences.zh: 溥求得井，有鼠自井出，投溥懷中，旋復入井。

translations.literal: Pu found the well; a rat emerged from it, leaped into his bosom, and then went back down the well.
translations.idiomatic: Pu found the well; a rat emerged from it, leaped into his bosom, and then went back down the well.

sentences.zh: 汲井索之，母屍在焉。

translations.literal: They drew water from the well and searched with ropes; his mother's corpse was there.
translations.idiomatic: They drew water from the well and searched with ropes; his mother's corpse was there.

sentences.zh: 哀呼不自勝，乃具棺斂，即其地以葬。

translations.literal: He cried out in grief beyond bearing, then prepared a coffin and shroud and buried her on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He cried out in grief beyond bearing, then prepared a coffin and shroud and buried her on the spot.

sentences.zh: 溥卒，子孫世襲指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Pu died, his descendants inherited the post of Vice Commander in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu died, his descendants inherited the post of Vice Commander in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：文輝、司馬任寄股肱，葉旺、馬雲效著邊域；

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Wenhui and Sima were entrusted as right-hand men; Ye Wang and Ma Yun won distinction on the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Wenhui and Sima were entrusted as right-hand men; Ye Wang and Ma Yun won distinction on the frontier;

sentences.zh: 大亨以端直見思，郭雲以政績蒙寵。

translations.literal: Daheng was remembered for his integrity; Guo Yun was favored for his administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Daheng was remembered for his integrity; Guo Yun was favored for his administrative achievements.

sentences.zh: 他如蔡遷、王銘、甯正、金興旺輩，或善戰，或善守，或善撫綏，要皆一時良將也。

translations.literal: Others such as Cai Qian, Wang Ming, Ning Zheng, and Jin Xingwang—some skilled in fighting, some in holding cities, some in pacification—were all fine generals of their age.
translations.idiomatic: Others such as Cai Qian, Wang Ming, Ning Zheng, and Jin Xingwang—some skilled in fighting, some in holding cities, some in pacification—were all fine generals of their age.

sentences.zh: 蓋明運初興，人材蔚起，鐵券、丹符之外，其可稱者猶如此。

translations.literal: When the Ming destiny first rose, talent flourished everywhere; apart from iron certificates and red writs, those who could be praised were still as numerous as this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming destiny first rose, talent flourished everywhere; apart from those granted iron certificates and red writs, those worthy of praise were still as numerous as this.

sentences.zh: 以視詩人《兔罝》之詠，何多讓哉。

translations.literal: Compared with the poet's praise in "The Rabbit Snares," how much would they have to yield?
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the poet's praise in "The Rabbit Snares," how much would they have to yield?
